blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Communicating in difficult moments is the single most revealing skill an executive can be tested on. In calm periods, almost any message will do; in a crisis, what you say and how you say it shapes everything from employee trust to share price. Few communication challenges are less forgiving.

Three principles hold up remarkably well under pressure. Tell the truth as clearly as you can, including what you do not yet know. Acknowledge the human impact before you explain the business rationale. And, crucially, never let the first message from leadership be heard second-hand, through the press or through a leaked memo.

Paradoxically, leaders who are willing to show controlled vulnerability in these moments tend to emerge with stronger trust, not weaker. It is the executives who retreat behind corporate language, refuse to acknowledge the cost to real people, or disappear for three weeks behind a communications team, who find it hardest to rebuild the relationship afterwards.

items.q: According to the text, when is an executive's communication skill most revealing?
options: In calm periods, when messages are routine
In a crisis, when what you say shapes trust and share price
items.why: "in a crisis, what you say and how you say it shapes everything from employee trust to share price."

items.q: In what order does the text say a leader should communicate?
options: Business rationale first, then the human impact
The human impact first, then the business rationale
Share price implications first, then everything else
What you already know first, hiding what you do not
items.why: "Acknowledge the human impact before you explain the business rationale."

items.q: The phrase "Few communication challenges are less forgiving" suggests that…
options: crisis communication punishes missteps unusually harshly
most executives find crises easy to handle
items.why: Inferência: "less forgiving" = perdoa pouco; poucos desafios punem erros tão duramente quanto uma crise.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Admitting what you do not yet know strengthens credibility.
Polished corporate language is the safest response in a crisis.
The human cost deserves acknowledgement before the numbers.
Leadership should speak before a leaked memo does.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que quem se esconde atrás de "corporate language" tem mais dificuldade de reconstruir a relação.

items.q: What does the word "Paradoxically" signal about controlled vulnerability?
options: That it produces the opposite of the expected result — more trust, not less
That it is a contradiction leaders should avoid
That vulnerability and trust are unrelated
That it only works with external audiences
items.why: Inferência: espera-se que mostrar vulnerabilidade enfraqueça; o paradoxo é que, controlada, ela fortalece a confiança.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver enquanto ele ajuda o CEO a preparar o comunicado. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, before we touch a single sentence, let's be clear about what this message has to do. Two thousand roles are affected. Those aren't figures on a slide — they are people who will read this at their kitchen tables tonight, and they will remember exactly how we spoke to them.

So here is my strong recommendation. You go first, and you go in person. If a journalist or a leaked memo reaches them before you do, we have already lost the room, and no follow-up will win it back.

Open with the human impact. Not the market conditions, not the restructuring logic — the people. Then, and only then, explain why this was unavoidable. And where you genuinely don't have an answer yet, say so plainly. "We don't know that yet, and we'll tell you the moment we do" earns more trust than a confident guess that turns out wrong.

One last thing. Don't disappear after this. The temptation will be to hand everything to communications and go quiet for a fortnight. That silence gets read as indifference every time. Stay visible, take the hard questions, and keep your composure even when they are angry with you.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Oliver insist the CEO must do about being the first to speak?
options: Let communications release the message first
Go first, and in person, before any leak or journalist reaches staff
Wait for the market to react before speaking
Send a written memo only, to avoid difficult questions
items.why: "You go first, and you go in person. If a journalist or a leaked memo reaches them before you do, we have already lost the room."

items.q: How does Oliver say the CEO should open the message?
options: With the human impact — the people
items.why: "Open with the human impact. Not the market conditions… the people."

items.q: What does Oliver recommend when the CEO does not yet have an answer?
options: Offer a confident guess to look decisive
Say plainly that they don't know yet and will tell people when they do
items.why: "where you genuinely don't have an answer yet, say so plainly… earns more trust than a confident guess that turns out wrong."

items.q: Why does Oliver warn against going quiet for a fortnight afterwards?
options: Because silence from the top is read as indifference
Because the CEO would miss board meetings
Because communications cannot handle the workload
Because the press prefers frequent statements
items.why: Inferência: "That silence gets read as indifference every time" — o sumiço é interpretado como descaso.

items.q: What is Oliver's underlying attitude toward showing feeling in this message?
options: He thinks emotion should be hidden behind polished language
He believes acknowledging people's feelings, while staying composed, builds trust
He wants the CEO to avoid any personal exposure
He treats the human side as a distraction from the numbers
items.why: Inferência: ele pede impacto humano primeiro e serenidade sob pressão — reconhecer sem perder a compostura.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Even as the questions turned hostile, she kept her composure." Composure means…
items.why: Composure = serenidade / compostura: manter o autocontrole mesmo sob pressão.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "He led with the ___ — the layoffs and the families affected — before he ever mentioned costs."
items.why: Human impact = impacto humano: o efeito sobre as pessoas, colocado antes dos números.

items.q: "The plan leaked before the town hall, and by morning it was a leaked memo in every inbox." A leaked memo is…
options: an internal document made public without authorisation
items.why: Leaked memo = memorando vazado: documento interno tornado público sem autorização.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "By admitting what they didn't yet know, the board began to ___ after months of doubt."
items.why: Rebuild trust = reconstruir confiança: o resultado de comunicar com honestidade.

items.q: "He hid behind corporate language, so nobody believed a word." Corporate language here means…
options: vague, impersonal jargon that avoids real meaning
items.why: Corporate language = linguagem corporativa: jargão impessoal e vago que esvazia a mensagem.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem quando a liderança comunica em momentos difíceis. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CEO had to sign off on every line before it went out." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "When the questions got tough, he refused to gloss over the job losses." To gloss over means to…
options: treat something serious as if it were unimportant
items.why: Gloss over = passar por cima, minimizar algo grave como se fosse trivial.

items.q: "Leadership promised support but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry the promise to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi prometido; aqui, o oposito — não cumpriram.

items.q: "A vague statement won't move the needle on employee trust." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir uma diferença perceptível.

items.q: "He was tempted to lie low until the storm passed." To lie low means to…
options: stay out of sight and avoid attention
items.why: Lie low = ficar na moita, evitar exposição — exatamente o que a lição desaconselha a um líder.
